fetich: charm or object believed to hold spiritual power over people
heathen: person who does not follow Christianity or any recognized religion
heathenism: state of being non-Christian; worship of idols or spirits
palaver: public meeting or discussion held to settle a dispute
cannibal: person who eats the flesh of other human beings
consanguinity: blood relationship between people descended from a common ancestor
ordeal: severe test, often dangerous, used to determine guilt or innocence
creditor: person to whom money or goods are owed
debtor: person who owes money or goods to another
hostage: person held as security until a promise is kept
forfeit: lose something as a penalty for a wrong or broken agreement
restitution: payment or restoring of goods to make up for harm done
dowry: goods or money passed from a husband's side to the bride's family
furlough: leave of absence granted to a missionary returning home
palm-oil: oil pressed from palm fruit, traded as a valuable product
ivory: hard white tusk of elephants, traded as a valuable product
rubber: elastic gum from tropical vines, collected and sold for trade
canoe: narrow boat, paddled or poled, used on rivers and coasts
polygamy: custom of a man having more than one wife at a time
monogamy: custom of having only one wife or husband at a time
polytheism: belief in and worship of many gods
monopoly: exclusive control of a trade or product by one party
animism: belief that spirits dwell in animals, plants, objects, and natural things
aboriginal: original inhabitant of a land, living there from earliest times
primitive: simple, early, or undeveloped in form and manner of life
sociology: scientific study of human society and how people live together
theology: study of religious belief and the nature of God
arcana: secret or mysterious knowledge known only to a few
cognate: related by common origin, such as words or languages
superstition: belief in magic or supernatural causes not based on reason
witchcraft: use of secret supernatural power to harm or control others
sacrifice: offering of animals, food, or goods to please a god or spirit
appease: calm an angry spirit or person by giving offerings or concessions
invoke: call upon a god or spirit for help or protection
reverence: deep respect, often with religious awe, toward a person or power
forefathers: ancestors who lived in earlier generations of a family
vices: wicked or immoral habits and faults of character
virtues: good moral qualities and habits of right living
denounce: publicly condemn or accuse someone of wrongdoing
commend: praise or recommend someone for good conduct
falsehood: statement known to be untrue; a lie
cohabit: live together as husband and wife without a legal marriage
minor: person below legal age, not yet responsible under the law
supremacy: highest power or authority over all others
eminence: high rank or position of honour and distinction
degradation: loss of moral dignity or lowering of status and character
dialect: local variety of a language with its own words and sounds
vocabulary: set of words known or used in a particular language
derivative: word or thing formed or developed from another source
mourning: expressing grief and sorrow, especially after a death
adjacent: lying next to or close to something else
sincerity: genuine honesty in one's beliefs, words, or feelings
inherit: receive property or position from someone who has died
evolution: gradual development of a thing from simpler earlier forms
gratified: pleased or satisfied by something that has happened
abused: treated cruelly or wrongly, or used improperly
admission: confession that something is true, often a fault
beasts: animals, especially large wild or domestic four-footed creatures
lapse: gradual falling away or slipping into a worse condition
